concerns.text: Constitution Principle II (Verified Accuracy) is cited as 'mandates checksums for all raw data'. However, Principle II in the constitution explicitly defines 'Verified Accuracy' as the requirement for external citations to be verified by the Reference-Validator Agent against primary sources (title-token-overlap ≥ 0.7). The checksum requirement belongs to Principle III (Data Hygiene). This misalignment creates a false mapping where the plan claims to satisfy a principle it does not actually address, violating the 'Constitution-Check coverage' requirement.

Constitution Principle V (Versioning Discipline) is described as 'Content hashes for artifacts will be managed by the execution agent'. The constitution explicitly states that 'Every artifact under this project carries a content hash' and that the 'Advancement-Evaluator Agent invalidates stale review records'. The plan's phrasing implies a passive role for the agent rather than the active versioning discipline required by the constitution, potentially leading to a failure in the 'Versioning Discipline' check.

The 'Complexity Tracking' table rejects 'Nested CV' as a 'scope addition in rejected tasks'. However, the 'research.md' artifact (which is part of the same design set) explicitly discusses 'Nested CV' in the context of 'Multiple Comparison Correction' and 'Sample Size & Power' without rejecting it. This creates an internal inconsistency between the plan's rejection of a methodology and the research document's consideration of it, confusing the implementation path.

The 'Technical Context' section lists 'pymatgen' as a primary dependency. However, the 'data-model.md' and 'contracts' sections rely on 'periodictable' for elemental properties (atomic radius, etc.). The plan does not clarify if 'pymatgen' is used for the same purpose or if it is redundant. If 'pymatgen' is not used for the specific descriptors defined in the data model, its inclusion in the plan's dependency list without a specific use-case reference creates a 'writing' inconsistency with the data model's implementation strategy.
